title: lifedraft input contract — universal (target shape, Track C / #602)
$comment: A dated balance sheet of entities. Facts (people/accounts/liabilities/properties/estate/cash_flows), beliefs (assumptions) and questions (decisions/sensitivity) are separate top-level namespaces. additionalProperties:false everywhere: an unknown key is a load error, not a silent drop. null means 'unknown'; a field is omitted only when structurally inapplicable to a given `kind` (enforced by allOf/if/then); 0 means exactly zero (DP#32). This file holds the JURISDICTION-AGNOSTIC shape only. countries/canada/input_schema.json (this repo's overlay, at schema/countries/canada/input_schema.json) supplies Canada-specific enums (account kinds, provinces, CPP/OAS, LIRA/LSIF/RESP/FHSA sub-shapes) and is COMPOSED with this file by input_contract.compose_schema() before validation -- see that module for the merge rule. This split is a deliberate, explicit user decision (see PR body): Atlas's original draft collapsed both files into one; the two-file split is kept because ~60 open jurisdiction issues and 3 in-flight country PRs (UK/Australia/WOTC) depend on the universal/overlay seam existing.

as_of.description: The date this snapshot of the balance sheet is true. The document's root date; balances/values may carry their own, more specific as_of (DP#1).

currency.description: ISO 4217. Only CAD supported today; enum, not free string, so a typo is a load error rather than a silently-wrong unit.

dollars.description: Whether every dollar figure in this document (facts AND assumptions) is nominal (as-stated) or real (constant purchasing power, base year below). A run cannot mix the two.

real_base_year.description: Required and meaningful only when dollars=real: the year whose price level all real figures are expressed in.

country.description: Study-level default. Package presence (DP#16) still drives which jurisdiction modules load; this field is the config-side declaration that must agree with it. The Canada overlay restricts this to the const 'canada'.

province.description: $defs/province is deliberately open (non-empty string) here; the Canada overlay replaces it with the closed 13-province/territory enum.

people.description: One entity per person, any generation. Generation, household membership and 'who is the study asking about' are all DERIVED from relationships + as_of, never declared by array position (#598).

accounts.description: Every registered/non-registered account, each owned by exactly one (or jointly by named) person(s) (#599). Replaces the household-singleton portfolio.accounts.* map.

liabilities.description: Every debt: mortgages, HELOCs, revolving lines of credit, term loans. balance and limit are always separate fields (#577/#601). Revolving kinds (heloc, line_of_credit) carry a `limit`; `collateral` (nullable) is what actually distinguishes secured from unsecured -- a HELOC is a line_of_credit with `collateral` set, not a different axis (#689).

properties.description: Every parcel of real property the family owns, replacing the property/house_comparison/rental_properties three-way split (#601).

cash_flows.description: Known/planned irregular income and expenses, dated. A FACT (already decided/known), not a belief.

household_budget.description: Issue #679: a FACT about ongoing cash flow -- what the household's own budget says it actually spends per year to live. Unlike assumptions.savings_rate (a stated intention/belief), this is measured from the household's own bank/credit statements. Optional and deliberately NOT in this schema's top-level `required` list (DP#16: auto-include on trigger data) -- a document that omits it simply cannot express the cash-flow solvency constraint (simulation_rules.apply_solvency), exactly as a document without house_value/mortgage_balance/margin_available cannot express the LTV explorer. Present-and-set is what engages the check; the check is never silently skipped once the data is there. The emergency RESERVE is a separate concept and lives under assumptions.emergency_reserve (#688): it is a policy (how many months to hold, and where), not a measured spend.

installments.description: Issue #759: fixed-term, zero-interest installment OBLIGATIONS -- a medical/dental/education payment plan structured as an up-front lump (already paid, not modelled here) followed by N equal monthly payments and an optional final balloon, at 0% interest, over a FIXED term. Neither a mortgage, nor revolving credit, nor a recurring living cost: it is non-negotiable under an income shock (it does NOT compress like discretionary spending -- contrast #761's discretionary split) AND it ENDS on its declared final payment date (it is not carried to the horizon the way household_budget.annual_living_costs is). Optional and deliberately NOT in this schema's top-level `required` list (DP#16: auto-include on trigger data) -- a document that omits it has no such plan, and the run is unchanged (the golden invariant must not move, DP#32). Each plan's payments fold into the solvency identity's debt-service term and the #758 reserve/runway sizing via simulation_rules.apply_installments, and STOP the year after the final payment.

equity_grants.description: Issue #768: private-company stock options / equity grants the household HOLDS but cannot count toward solvency or runway. A private, unvested, or strike-undetermined option grant is NOT a liquid asset -- it cannot be sold, cannot pay a mortgage, and realises only on a speculative, dated liquidity event that is outside the projection. The engine values every declared grant at $0 for ALL solvency / runway / decumulation metrics (#758, #679) and surfaces it as 'recorded, valued $0' so the household knows it was not silently dropped (DP#32: an absence-of-record is not a labelled $0). Optional and deliberately NOT in this schema's top-level `required` list (DP#16: auto-include on trigger data) -- a document that omits it has no such grants, and the run is unchanged (the golden invariant must not move). The block is RECORD-ONLY: it never feeds a simulation rule (no rule reads it), so its $0 contribution is by construction, and the output names each grant explicitly rather than inventing a value for it.

estate.description: Estate FACTS: elections currently in force and insurance in force. Mortality is a BELIEF and lives under assumptions.mortality (see migration-plan.md, hard decision #1).

assumptions.description: BELIEFS: what we assume about the world (returns, inflation, mortality, rate paths, tax-law overrides). Never a fact about the balance sheet.

decisions.description: QUESTIONS: what we are deciding between. The optimizer/scenario engine compares these candidates head-to-head. Absence of a candidate list means auto-discovery from trigger data (DP#16) is still permitted, but the schema always accepts an explicit list.

private_loans.description: Issue #832: private loans from an individual. The lender is either a declared household member or an individual outside the household (inline identity). Repayment/interest terms default to on_demand/on_demand -- a demand loan with no interest demanded is modeled as interest-free financing (no tax flow). When interest IS paid/payable, the lender accrues taxable income (in their bracket, if a household member) and the borrower's interest is deductible under ITA s.20(1)(c) when use=investment; a minor lender's interest is attributed to the borrower (s.74.2). Absent/empty = no private loans (the golden household). Supersedes #813.

gifts.description: Epic #841 bite 3: parent->child cash gifts that FUND a child's registered contributions (TFSA/FHSA/RRSP) beyond what the child's own small income can. A gift REDIRECTS after-tax savings from the household adult base to a child's OWN registered accounts (DP#18: money conserved -- the adult base drops by exactly what funds the child, no double-count). TAX FACTS modeled: an inter-vivos cash gift is NOT income to the child and NOT deductible to the donor (tax-free to both). The gift is applied EACH projection year and SELF-LIMITS: once the child's registered room is filled it funds nothing further (never spilling into non-registered -- that is asset location, bite 3 scope 3). Because registered room requires age 18+ AND registered growth is tax-sheltered, ITA s.74.1 minor-attribution has NO effect on a registered-room gift (no minor can hold the room, and there is no taxable income to attribute); it would matter only for a future non-registered gift to a minor. Absent/empty = no gifts (the golden household).

first_home_purchases.description: Issue #704: a household member (today: a CHILD) becomes a FIRST-TIME HOME BUYER in a given year, using the two instruments Canada provides for a first home. In that year the member's own FHSA is withdrawn TAX-FREE (qualifying withdrawal, the account closes) and up to $60,000 comes out of their own RRSP NON-TAXABLY under the Home Buyers' Plan (HBP), repaid over a 15-year schedule (countries/canada/fhsa.py, hbp_rules.py). Both proceeds fund the down payment (net worth conserved -- the FHSA drains tax-free, the HBP is a loan owed back to the member's own RRSP). Absent/empty = no first-home purchase (the golden household).

sensitivity.description: QUESTIONS (uncertainty dimension): named overlay presets and sweep ranges layered ACROSS every decision comparison, not decisions themselves (DP#5).

provenance.description: OPTIONAL sidecar (#660, epic #659 Track 1): every key is an RFC 6901 JSON Pointer into THIS document (e.g. "/accounts/0/balance/amount"), every value describes how that leaf is known. A leaf with NO entry here is `assumed` BY DEFINITION -- provenance.py's Provenance.confidence() returns "assumed" for any pointer absent from this object, so coverage is deliberately allowed to be incomplete; an author cannot dodge scrutiny by simply omitting an entry. Cross-document checks this schema fragment cannot express on its own (a pointer must resolve against the document; a plausible_range/domain must bracket/contain the leaf's actual current value) are enforced by provenance.load_provenance(), not by jsonschema.
